extraction.name: NeedleBench
extraction.description: NeedleBench is a comprehensive synthetic framework designed to assess retrieval and reasoning performance in bilingual long-context tasks with adaptive context lengths (e.g., 32k, 128k, and beyond). It systematically embeds key data points at varying depths to rigorously test models' capabilities in diverse settings. Tasks are categorized into two distinct scenarios: information-sparse (minimal relevant details embedded within extensive irrelevant text) and information-dense (the Ancestral Trace Challenge, where relevant information is continuously distributed throughout the context). The benchmark supports flexible context lengths (4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k, and beyond) and is bilingual (English and Chinese).
extraction.creator: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen (Tsinghua University, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
extraction.citeAs: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen. NeedleBench: Evaluating LLM Retrieval and Reasoning Across Varying Information Densities. Transactions on Machine Learning Research, 09/2025. arXiv:2407.11963v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark framework. Data is programmatically generated using algorithmic approaches. For information-sparse tasks, synthetic 'needles' (key information units) are embedded into haystack filler content. For the Ancestral Trace Challenge (ATC), synthetic family relationship datasets are generated algorithmically. The haystack for English tasks uses passages from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset, and for Chinese tasks, the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset is used.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: For information-sparse tasks, the haystack (filler) content is sourced from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset (for English) and the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset (for Chinese). The needles are synthetically generated abstract and fictional statements. For the ATC task, all data is synthetically generated using a defined algorithm with random name pools and relationship templates.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For information-sparse tasks, synthetic needles are inserted at varying depths within the haystack text to reach target context lengths (4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k, and beyond). A buffer is subtracted from the target context length when generating each input to mitigate instruction truncation. For the ATC task, relationship statements are shuffled to eliminate positional bias. Token lengths are measured using the GPT-4 tokenizer.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For each configuration, tests are repeated R=10 times to enhance result stability. A keyword-aware Exact Match (EM) metric is used for information-sparse tasks. For ATC, an exact match metric based on the model's output in \boxed{...} format is used. A buffer is subtracted from the target context length to ensure complete instructions are exposed to all models despite tokenizer differences.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Approximately 10% of observed errors from the ATC task were manually annotated by the authors, focusing on cases where the question type is 'identifying the eldest ancestor.' Error types identified include: under-thinking, partial understanding error, instruction following error, repetitive output error, hallucination error, and other errors. For small models (Qwen1.5-1.8B-Chat and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct), outputs were manually checked to identify false error rates caused by instruction-following errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Manual annotation of approximately 10% of ATC errors was performed to categorize error types. The 'false error rate' was computed for small models to identify cases where the model's answer was correct but marked wrong due to format non-compliance. Error type distribution was reported: under-thinking (60.2%), partial understanding (12.9%), instruction following (7.5%), repetitive output (7.5%), hallucination (7.5%), other (4.5%).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 tokenizer (tiktoken) for measuring token lengths; LMDeploy and vLLM for accelerating inference during evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: All codes and resources are publicly available at OpenCompass. The paper states all reproducible scripts, code, and datasets will be made available upon publication.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: NeedleBench provides critical insights and targeted evaluation tools essential for understanding and improving the long-context capabilities of LLMs, which are crucial for real-world applications such as legal document retrieval, academic research, and aggregating business intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is synthetic and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. The use of PaulGrahamEssays (English) and ChineseDomainModelingEval (Chinese) as haystack content may introduce linguistic or topical biases. Most models exhibit a performance gap between English and Chinese, with English scores typically higher, which may reflect biases in pretraining data distribution, tokenization strategies, or language-specific modeling approaches.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. The benchmark focuses on bilingual (English and Chinese) evaluation and may not generalize to other languages. The information-sparse tasks use filler content from specific datasets (PaulGrahamEssays, ChineseDomainModelingEval), which may not represent all domains. The ATC task uses synthetic family relationship chains, which may not capture all forms of real-world information-dense reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of large language models' long-context retrieval and reasoning capabilities. The benchmark is designed to assess bilingual (English and Chinese) performance across varying context lengths and information densities. It is intended for evaluating, not training, LLMs. It can be used to identify specific failure modes such as under-thinking, partial understanding, instruction following errors, repetitive output, and hallucination in long-context settings.
